title: Surge-aware GPU eviction strategy and phased capacity handoffs for Dedicated fleets
creator: Marina Chen
description:
Goal: Implement a surge-aware eviction strategy that coordinates GPU pool drains with the autoscaler and rollout gates to avoid service-level impact during LTS and minor version upgrades.

Background: Past upgrades experienced transient token-latency spikes and capacity shortfalls when many nodes drained simultaneously and horizontal autoscalers could not provision compatible replacement instances quickly. Current controllers assume steady-state drain windows; they don't consider burst ingress, regional capacity pressure, or cross-pool fallback costs.

Scope:
- Design a controller that computes an eviction budget in real-time using: current in-flight request distribution, per-pool SLO headroom, autoscaler warmup time, and upstream network/AKS/GKE provisioning signals.
- Implement phased handoffs: short canary evictions, opportunistic low-traffic wave, and guaranteed-preserve windows for high-SLO routes.
- Integrate with rollout gates (LTS channel checks + canary metrics) so that upgrade waves pause if 95th percentile latency or error-rate increase > configured thresholds.
- Provide fallbacks: model-variant routing to cheaper/quantized replicas and cross-region pool re-route when local capacity unavailable.
- Instrumentation and dashboards: token-level cost delta, per-route p50/p95 latency, drain-in-progress vs autoscaler-provisioned capacity.

Non-goals: scheduling placement optimizations unrelated to upgrades; the controller will call into existing eviction APIs rather than replace the scheduler core.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Autoscaler slow scale leads to long degradation windows. Mitigation: surface pre-warm recommendation metric and mark pools as "upgrade-blocking" to defer waves.
- Risk: Cross-pool routing could increase cost and RU. Mitigation: add cost-threshold gating and automated rollback triggers.

Deliverables: design doc, controller prototype, e2e upgrade runbook update, dashboard panels, and a staged rollout to dedicated canary pools.
